The report shows 28 checks and 0 failures, so I can't cite a failing check. I'm submitting three attacks, strongest first:

1. **Cold morning.** The camera has only 0.148 K of margin at -10 C. The design says it can launch down to -12 C, so -11.1 C should count as a go day, and I expect the camera to fall below its rating.
2. **High launch site.** The 75 m launch elevation was the agents' guess, because no site was given. At a 3800 m site the thinner air should push the 4.31 m/s landing speed above the 5 m/s limit.
3. **Longer search.** The 4 h search window is the schema default, not something the person asked for. If the payload lands somewhere hard to reach and the search takes two days, I expect the APRS 3S1P battery pack to run flat.

content.text: I'm blocking this design: the attack on the 4 h search-window default was confirmed. With a 48 h search, the LoRa 4S1P pack runs flat (power_margin -12.1 Wh), so the backup tracker dies when a search runs long. Finding: the request asks for an ELRS backup, but the design uses a Heltec LoRa beacon instead. The -11.1 C cold-morning attack was not confirmed, and the high-site attack was rejected unrun because I put a site name in the change. Details are in the verdict.

input.summary: BLOCKED by one confirmed attack: power_margin fails when recovery_window_h is 48 instead of the 4 h default the agents chose (regression balloon-1792886331-r1-1). The LoRa 4S1P bus needs 25.1 Wh and has 13.0 Wh at -10 C, a shortfall of 12.1 Wh, so the backup tracker dies during a long search after a landing in a tree, on closed land or in the foothills. Attacks that did not land: a -11.1 C ground day is not confirmed (part_temperature margin fell from +0.148 K to +0.092 K but still passes). The 3800 m high-site attack was rejected unrun because I wrongly included a launch.name string, so it remains untested; the landing_speed margin of +0.69 m/s was computed at an elevation the agents assumed (75 m). FINDING on a locked value: the request says 'APRS tracking with ELRS backup' and the locked mission says 'APRS primary tracking with ELRS backup', but design.trackers[1] is a Heltec LoRa32 V3 plus Matek M10 sending its own LoRa beacon on 915 MHz under Part 97. That is not ExpressLRS, the request is not met as written, and no check measures it. Non-blocking concerns: the runcam5-orange -10..40 C rating is marked 'rating assumed' and the camera passes the cold end by about 0.1 K, so a sourced datasheet value could flip part_temperature. The declared launch window goes down to -12 C against a modelled limit of -12.9 C. recovery_probability is 0.906 against 0.9 and is judged on assumed winds because spec.wind is empty, although the design passed one run on a GFS forecast. On hard ground the rack shelf reaches 77.7 MPa against PETG's 20 MPa allowable; this case is not judged, and the check only says 'land away from roads'. The Hanford site itself is an assumption. Walked: omission (finding only, no check exposes it), environment and units_sign were tested. Interference, copy consistency, sourcing and regulatory limits had nothing to attack, but I did not look up catalog stock to support the sourcing call. Model validity is treated as clear; the hard-ground shelf case is noted above.
